profile.name: Mobilerun
profile.description: mobilerun.ai provides a hosted, 24/7 AI‑powered mobile automation platform that lets developers and teams control real Android and iOS devices through natural language or API calls. Users can provision fleets of phones with residential IPs, eSIMs, and unique phone numbers, then run agents that tap, swipe, type, and read screens just like a human. The service includes mobilerun VA, an always‑on virtual assistant, and mobilerun Connect for secure network identity. With a single SDK and API key, customers can automate tasks such as app interactions, data extraction, and social media posting at scale, while the open‑source mobilerun framework lets them run agents locally or in the cloud. Backed by a16z and Y Combinator, mobilerun.ai targets developers, QA teams, and enterprises needing reliable, stealthy mobile automation without managing hardware themselves.
profile.slogan: One platform. The whole mobile stack.

notes: Hook caption drifted from the planned one. The script has 'my AI agent tests real phones, then reports back', but the plan and the reference's 'now ... if it has a question' phrasing call for 'my AI agent now runs tests on real phones and tells me when it's done'. The reference caption is a full 3-line premise, and the shortened one loses the 'tells me' payoff.

Invented UI content. 'Launch app, Open Cart, Checkout' on the task card and live view are not in the brief. The brief's only step names are Launch Stripe, Verify Face ID, Open Payouts and Export JSON, for a different task. A fake checkout flow makes the demo less true.
Timing is off the reference's beats. The script's 4.5 / 2 / 4 / 6 puts the 'Mobilerun.' name beat at 4.5 s, not about 4.3 s. The reference is 4.3 / 2.1 / 4.2 / 6.1.

Beat 3 crams five chat lines ('Open our app, test checkout', 'Passed · 14s', 'Now test it on 20 devices', 'Spinning up sessions…', '20 tests passed · 31s') into 4 s. That breaks the reference's calm, static feel, where attention stays on the voice. Show fewer changes so the phone stays readable.

Beat 4's screen stacks too much: the live view step list, a webhook line, and the '20 tests passed' result. Beat 4 should show the live view/recording with 'Each step goes to your webhook' and the result, with nothing invented.

notes: lint: 6 beats vs the reference's 4: keep its beats one for one

Beat count drifts: 6 beats vs the reference's 4 (hook / reveal / demo / payoff). The reference timing is 0-4.3, 4.3-6.4, 6.4-10.6, 10.6-16.7. Split proof, offer and CTA into their own beats and the pacing no longer matches. Keep it to four beats.

Beat 1 opens with 'Good news.' That is the reference's line from the status-report beat, moved into the hook. The reference gives 'Claude Phone.' its own reveal beat, and 'Good news.' belongs to the report that follows. Keeping the voice at 0 s is fine, but the beat order should follow the reference.
Beat 2 is a one-word, 1 s reveal ('Mobilerun.'). The reference reveal runs about 2 s. It is rushed and reads as filler, so give it the reference's length and let it land.
Beat 3 packs 17 words into 4.5 s. That is about 227 wpm, so it is at the limit of the reference's pace. The deadpan polite feel suffers if any more is added.

The proof, offer and CTA are spread over three short beats (3.5 s, 3 s, 2 s). The result reads like a rapid ad checklist, not one continuous deadpan status report. Merge them into the closing payoff beat, as the reference does with its report plus 'That's all. Bye.'
The 'no extra charges' offer line is true to the brief but pushes beat 5 past 3 s. Trim it to '60 device minutes' so the closing beat can be said cleanly.

events.message: Campaign started: 2 videos, 2 shots each, google/veo-3.1

Research plan: AI mobile automation cloud; competitors BrowserStack, AWS Device Farm, Genymotion, GeeLark, Sauce Labs; searching AI agent keeps failing on app, automate phone tasks with AI, day in the life QA engineer, AI agent on a real phone, tools I wish I knew sooner

Scout: No Mobilerun-relevant breakout in this wave. The high views-per-follower hits are off-topic: AI-fear and scam clips (sophiajamis_, nerd.girl.loser, cottage.beansoup), funny iPhone/Android skits, and a storytime series. Two are closer to the buyer. studywithtay2 (2.2k followers, 4.7M views, 0.49 saves per like, 'I didn't believe it at first... using this') is a tool-reaction format that sells. kate.voice.ai (1k followers, 2.3M views, face-to-camera 'my virtual assistant' with clones 3.7) shows an AI assistant pitched on camera works. Missing entirely: any review, demo or comparison of an AI agent that operates a phone, any QA or growth-team creator talking to camera, and any call to action or link-in-bio. Digging into "AI phone assistant review" (tiktok), "I tried AI that uses my phone" (tiktok), "AI automation tool review" (instagram), "phone farm multiple accounts" (tiktok), "AI test automation review" (youtube)
Research done: 100 short videos to rank, 16 live ads, 2 Reddit threads, 17 keywords (42/44 sources)
A provider is busy at style (naive: the model returned a malformed tool call); retrying with backoff for up to about 30 minutes
Product brief: software, "Real Android and iPhone cloud phones that an AI agent can tap, swipe and type on, so you describe a task in plain language and it runs." (0 visuals)
